cells.tense: What you feel here has settled deep enough to sit with, and you are sitting with it.
cells.ask: Spend one evening with nothing decided, letting what you know stay the whole of it, and notice who you are on the other side of that hour.
cells.core:
The feeling has gone all the way down and you're not hauling it back up. You sit with what you actually know even when it's quiet and unglamorous, even when nobody would notice you doing anything at all. That calm isn't numbness. It's feeling that found its floor.

Around you there's clearing — some things finished, and you're not standing on them anymore. Steadiness like this is what lets you look at what's gone without flinching, and it's rarer than it sounds. The edge here isn't staying; it's letting the sitting be enough for one evening, deciding nothing, and letting what you know move you when it moves you.
cells.sheetLine: You sit with what you know instead of forcing the next move.

cells.tense: Some part of you is already living after this ends, bracing for what comes next before it is here.
cells.ask: Close one drawer you've been holding open for later — keep or let go, today — and leave it closed until tomorrow.
cells.core:
You're further ahead than the ending is. In your head the clearing already happened and you're over there running the next version — what you'll arrange once it's done, who you're becoming after. The feeling doesn't get to finish arriving, because you keep leaving first. When this part of you is going well, you stay with what's actually in front of you and let the next thing wait its turn.

What's ending here runs on its own clock and won't take yours. Waiting isn't sitting still; it's the part you can't rush, the way a crop ripens without help. If you close one drawer you've been keeping ajar, the room genuinely gets emptier, and you find out whether you're clearing or decorating.

cells.tense: The ending is already behind you, and you are still speaking about it as one you have not reached.
cells.ask: Tell one person who was there that it's over — say it plainly, once — and let that sentence be the whole repair.
cells.core:
Where you stand, the ending happened. You describe it as though it's still ahead. The settled feeling shows up too — a good moment, a flash of how light it is not to carry this — and you pass those off as mood. So the room you're in keeps all the old furniture in place. When this part of you is working, you name what's finished right when you feel it.

This isn't about pushing feeling into a quiet place. Your read on it went scattered; the work is gathering it. Whatever you think of the outcome, say it out loud once to someone, and the question stops being open.

cells.tense: The clearing is already underway, and you watch it happen instead of taking it as your own choice.
cells.ask: Describe the ending to one person as your own decision, out loud, and hear how that lands in the room.
cells.core:
The ending is already moving through your days. Some weight has come off, some things quietly stopped, and you notice more than you let on. What you say out loud runs the other way: that it's time doing it, or circumstances, or they pulled away first. The ending is yours and your account of it isn't.

You can go one layer down here, closer rather than farther out. Sit with what you actually know about this ending before you turn it into a story about timing. Saying it as your choice will sound odd in your mouth; that's how you know it's the true one.
